P2_budget_vs_gpu_busy._claim: the budget must not bind artificially (D102)
P2_budget_vs_gpu_busy.diagnosis: the THIRD TERM is the problem and it is a double count. per_queue * queued_ahead is the LATENCY this request SUFFERS because other requests' work is in front of it, not GPU time this request consumes. Charging it bills the same GPU-seconds once per request queued behind them: with k requests of u tokens in flight the queue charge grows as u^2 k^2 / 2 while the real work grows linearly. On the planner side the same term is CORRECT, because there it prices the delay a candidate IMPOSES on others, which is exactly what it measures
P2_budget_vs_gpu_busy.intercept_is_not_the_driver: charging the 0.0678 s intercept to every request makes a 1-frame dashcam append 2.0x dearer and a 21-frame one 1.1x dearer, which alone would not starve anything
P2_budget_vs_gpu_busy.verdict: FAIL: under the ruling's formula as written the budget binds ARTIFICIALLY. 10612 refusals (10593 dashcam) against 288 under work-only, and plan_state reaches 0 decisions against 2038. The arm is MORE starved than it was under the old touch price, for a different reason. The rerun is HELD
